newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mostly firmer.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mostly firmer.

text.p: Feb 28 - Most IMM currency futures ended firmer. Yen neared highs as marks, Swiss fr eased. Talk of month-end repatriation also aided yen. Mex peso built gains on ideas Pres Clinton would recertify Mexico as drug-war ally, shortcovering from Thursday's drop, and rise in Mexican short rates. Pound up on crosses, ideas UK Conservative election losses factored in. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
The yen also managed to regain its footing as the dollar returned below 121.00 and struggled briefly to stay above 120.00 level, brokers said.
"I was looking for the yen to fall more," said a sheepish currency floor broker. "But there's not much support dollar-wise below that (120.00) until you get close to 119.00."
The 121.00, 120.00 and 119.00 cash dollar/yen levels would be roughly equivalent to $0.008281, $0.008350 and $0.008420, respectively, in March yen futures.

Sterling rose, also buoyed on crosses and pre-weekend covering, with some brokers saying the unit already may have adjusted to expectations that U.K.'s ruling Conservative government will lose more ground to the opposition Labor Party.

Earlier in the session, marks had firmed vis-a-vis the pound when one fund was seen buying a total of 2,000 March marks against sales of sterling, possibly unwinding a position taken earlier this week, brokers said.
The Mexican peso reversed course and advanced, buoyed by reports that President Clinton would recertify Mexico as a partner in the war on drugs.

The official announcement was expected after futures closed Friday. U.S. Senator Dianne Feinstein, a California Democrat, said she would lead an effort in Congress to disapprove Mexico's recertification.
Traders also tied the peso's gains to shortcovering from Thursday's dramatic slide as well as a rise in short-term Mexican interest rates Friday.

Currencies showed muted response to the downward revised U.S. fourth-quarter gross domestic product or to the February Chicago purchasing managers index, which firmed slightly although employment and prices paid components slipped.

March yen settled up $0.000045 at $0.008343, marks eased $0.0002 to $0.5926, Swiss francs dipped $0.0012 to $0.6783, sterling rose $0.0046 to $1.6292, Canadian dollar added $0.0004 to $0.7319, Australian dollar rose $0.0022 to $0.7783, and the Mexican peso gained $0.000950 to $0.125200.
